entities.summary:
Josceline de Bohon or Bohun was an Anglo-Norman religious leader born around 1150 in Normandy, France, and died on November 25, 1184. A key figure in the development of the Cistercian Order, Josceline played a crucial role in the spread of monasticism throughout the British Isles, particularly in Ireland and Scotland. His leadership and vision helped establish the Cistercian network, which would go on to shape the religious and cultural landscape of the region for centuries to come.




Josceline's significance extends beyond his religious influence, as he was also a prominent landowner and politician in medieval England. His family connections to the Norman nobility and his own roles as a sheriff and lord of the manor demonstrate the complex web of power and patronage that defined medieval society.




As a leading figure in the Cistercian Order, Josceline de Bohon's legacy can be seen in the many monasteries and abbeys he founded or helped establish, including the famous Melrose Abbey in Scotland. His influence on the development of monasticism in the British Isles has had a lasting impact on the region's art, architecture, and cultural heritage.




Despite the passing of time, Josceline de Bohon's story remains a fascinating chapter in the history of medieval England. His remarkable life, marked by both spiritual dedication and political ambition, serves as a testament to the complex and multifaceted nature of human experience.
